name: POST /api/hdk-video/edits — hdk-video-editor
description: Accepts a video trim from an offline-capable HDK client and queues it as hdk-video.trim.applied.v1 for hdk-sync's conflict resolver (event-sourcing for image/video, lww for scanner). Answers 202 Accepted rather than 200/201: nothing is created synchronously — the route appends an audit entry and returns. When blob_id AND op are both present the op is appended to media.blob.edit_history; either one alone is silently ignored, so a caller sending only op sees a 202 and no edit. device_uuid is the sole required field — everything else is optional, so a payload that omits it is the only request shape this route rejects. Audit emission is best-effort and swallowed on failure, so a 202 does NOT prove the event was written; verify audit.entry rather than trusting the status. `op` is deliberately absent from fieldEnums: it is free-form jsonb, not an enum-backed field. sdk-media's appendEditOp takes Record<string, unknown> and appends it verbatim to media.blob.edit_history (blobService.ts:348) — no validator, no CHECK constraint and no enumerated set exists, so an op of any shape returns 202. The source header names crop/rotate/annotate (image) and trim (video) as the INTENDED operations, but nothing enforces them; listing them as accepted values would tell QA a constraint exists that does not.

errorCases.when: Authorization header absent or not in Bearer form - gateway default-deny authGate onRequest hook (AUTH_GATE_MODE=enforce)
Bearer token fails JWT verification in the gateway authGate
the request body has no device_uuid - the route's only validation

testCases.name: Queue a video trim for an attested device
